observations.text: SP, due to a late initiation of the deceleration and configuration schedule, did not bring the A/C into landing configuration timely and correctly, and gear and flaps were still in transit at the start of the final segment. Airspeed exceeded the briefed value by 30 knots and altitude diverged by 400 feet, beyond the +/-20 knot and +/-300 foot limits. The IP directed the configuration sequence and executed part of the approach so that the formation could continue safely.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not check the proper configuration of the wingman and did not monitor the wingman's position before the final segment. Lead airspeed decayed 25 knots below the briefed approach speed and heading diverged 15 degrees from the inbound course, beyond the +/-20 knot and +/-10 degree limits. The IP directed the corrections and flew part of the approach so that the wingman could regain position.

SP executed the formation approach as leader within the desired standards for the Training Section, completing the landing configuration and the wingman configuration check after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude reached 300 feet and airspeed 20 knots from the briefed values, at the limit of the allowed deviation, with errors recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the block - earlier initiation of the configuration sequence and prompt self-correction are expected to improve.

SP, without prompting from the IP, brought the A/C into landing configuration timely and correctly and checked the proper configuration of the wingman before the final segment. Minor deviations of 200 feet in altitude and 15 knots in airspeed were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the formation approach as leader with accuracy and speed, bringing the A/C into landing configuration at the briefed point and confirming in time that the wingman was properly configured and in position for the approach flown. Altitude was maintained within 150 feet, airspeed within 10 knots and heading within 5 degrees of the briefed values, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP led the formation approach with exceptional precision, sequencing the landing configuration, the wingman configuration check and the position assessment ahead of every briefed point. Deviations were negligible, with altitude held within 50 feet, airspeed within 5 knots and heading within 2 degrees, and lead calls were clear and timely throughout the recovery. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect power and speed brake technique in the descent, did not establish the briefed approach parameters and did not bring the A/C into landing configuration at the briefed point. Airspeed exceeded the briefed value by 35 knots and altitude diverged by 450 feet, well beyond the +/-20 knot and +/-300 foot limits, and the wingman could not hold position. The IP directed the parameters and executed part of the approach.

SP, due to failure to exercise formation lead responsibilities during the recovery, did not check the proper configuration of the wingman and did not assert that the wingman had reached the proper position before the approach was continued. Heading diverged 20 degrees from the inbound course and altitude by 500 feet, exceeding the +/-10 degree and +/-300 foot limits. The IP intervened, directed the pattern re-entry and flew part of the approach.

SP, due to a non-standardized configuration flow, did not lower gear and flaps at the briefed point of the formation approach, and the wingman configuration check was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. Airspeed reached 20 knots and altitude 300 feet from the briefed values, at the limit of the allowed deviation. Errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on the inbound leg, did not monitor the wingman and did not assert that the wingman had reached the proper position for the approach to be executed. Heading was allowed to diverge 10 degrees from the inbound course, at the limit of the allowed deviation, and was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. Recognition and correction of the deviation were delayed.

SP executed the formation approach as leader within the desired standards, bringing the A/C into landing configuration correctly and checking the wingman's configuration without IP's intervention. However, airspeed twice reached 15 knots from the briefed value and altitude 200 feet, before being recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter airspeed control and earlier lead calls are expected to improve.

SP brought the A/C into landing configuration timely and correctly, checked the proper configuration of the wingman and asserted in time that the wingman was in the proper position for the approach flown. Altitude was maintained within 150 feet, airspeed within 10 knots and heading within 5 degrees of the briefed values, with accuracy and speed and without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP led the formation approach with exceptional precision, configuring the A/C and confirming the wingman's configuration and position ahead of every briefed point. Deviations were negligible, with altitude held within 50 feet, airspeed within 5 knots and heading within 2 degrees of the briefed values, and formation lead responsibilities were exercised above the level expected for the block. Above end of block MIF achieved.
